audience.programmeDescription: Environmental Sciences at Wageningen combines natural science, social science and technology to investigate pollution, climate change, resource use and environmental solutions. The programme is taught in English and remains rooted in the natural sciences.

curriculum.routeLabel: Common academic core; Interdisciplinary Environmental Challenges context
curriculum.limitation: The listed curriculum totals 180 EC. Only the independent 105 EC common core is assessed. The further 75 EC is unassessed, including the specialisation and thesis; the current eligible-chair preparation for the illustrated choices remains unverified. Genuine open study remains unassigned.

componentNotes.common-math-choice: This example uses Mathematics Applied: Introduction for VWO Mathematics A. Students with Mathematics B take Statistics 1 instead; the choice follows prior preparation and study advice. This component is outside the assessed 105 EC common core.
componentNotes.common-solutions: General, laboratory and fieldwork safety are non-credit requirements for the relevant practical activities. They are not added to the 180 EC.
componentNotes.spec-nexus: The selected specialisation combines this 6 EC nexus course with 12 EC of social-science and 12 EC of natural-science/technology options. Other permitted combinations may use 6–18 EC in each of those groups, with up to 6 EC of optional quantitative methods, while keeping 30 EC in total. This component is outside the assessed 105 EC common core.
componentNotes.spec-law: This example selects the first two listed social-science options: International and EU Environmental Law and Environmental Economics. This is one permitted choice, not a claim that both are compulsory for every student in the specialisation. This component is outside the assessed 105 EC common core.
componentNotes.spec-renewable: This example selects Renewable Energy Technologies and the paired Organic Chemistry 1 and Environmental Organic Chemistry units from the natural-science/technology group. Laboratory safety applies to the chemistry practicals. This component is outside the assessed 105 EC common core.
componentNotes.common-project: WUR requires a 12 EC international, field-based transdisciplinary project with a commissioner and local stakeholders. It assumes at least 60 EC from the first two years and requires fieldwork safety. Separate UCR projects do not reproduce this coordinated course.
componentNotes.common-micro-tox: WUR combines microbial cells, diversity, growth and metabolism with a microbiology practical and chemical toxicity/risk. UCR Life Science Laboratory has a direct partial practical relationship through microbial culture, identification and molecular methods; it does not reproduce all microbial physiology or toxicology.
componentNotes.common-skills-academy: WUR integrates skills across courses and years, emphasising personal leadership, reflection and a portfolio. UCR PPD supplies a partial relationship in reflective personal/academic development and societal collaboration, with a different duration and structure.
componentNotes.common-air: WUR studies pollutant emissions, atmospheric transport, chemical conversion, deposition and health effects with models and observations. General climate-change study does not reproduce this air-quality sequence.
componentNotes.spec-env-organic: WUR studies organic pollutants, their reactivity, breakdown and environmental stability after Organic Chemistry 1. UCR’s metal recovery and soil-remediation work does not reproduce this dedicated organic-chemistry sequence. This component is outside the assessed 105 EC common core.
componentNotes.free-choice: Thirty EC remains available for a minor and/or individually chosen electives. An optional 12 or 18 EC internship would use part of this space; no internship is required in this example. This component is outside the assessed 105 EC common core.
componentNotes.thesis: The required individual thesis is 12 EC. Entry requires at least 102 BES credits, all 60 first-year credits, and preparation for the chosen chair group. The applicable chair-group preparation for this course combination still needs confirmation. This component is outside the assessed 105 EC common core.
componentNotes.common-chem1: WUR teaches physical-chemical foundations including thermal motion, driving forces, equilibrium, adsorption, acids/bases and kinetics. UCR environmental geochemistry directly addresses part of the aqueous-equilibrium, adsorption and acid/base subject and laboratory methods; the complete physical-chemistry sequence differs.

audience.comparisonExplanation: This qualified comparison assesses the confirmed 105 EC common academic core. All 180 listed EC remain visible, but the 30 EC specialisation, 3 EC background-dependent choice, 12 EC thesis and 30 EC genuine open study are unassessed. The UCR programmes provide broader environmental-science responses, with different laboratory, ecological, quantitative or governance priorities. They do not reproduce the entire general-chemistry, toxicology, air-quality or coordinated international field-project sequence. Thesis-chair preparation and complete graduation eligibility remain unverified.
